title_en: How Many Teams Will Be in Avengers: Doomsday? A Lot
summary_en: How many super teams will be in Avengers: Doomsday? A lot...
body_en:
With the new “final” Avengers: Doomsday trailer as well as the recent reveal from Marvel of who exactly makes up Sam Wilson’s Avengers team in the film , some of the more casual fans out there might think, “OK, you have a Captain America, an Asgardian, a bug guy, and a couple of others. That’s our new Avengers.” To which the less than casual, more, shall we say, ardent fans will scream, “BRUSH UP ON YOUR MCU, MAN!” Because you know what? Doomsday will definitely be featuring more than just a simple, single team of Earth’s Mightiest Heroes.
Yeah, we’ve got X-Men, we’ve got Fantastic Four, and we’ve got a whole lot more too. So let’s take a look at all the super teams that will show up in the new movie when it hits (that we know of so far, anyway)...
(Note: We of course don’t know every character who’ll pop up in Doomsday, or how the events of the film will play out, so there could be – and likely will be – some flux to these team line-ups as the story unfolds. Exciting!)
The MCU version of the Avengers haven’t actually had that many adventures when you think about it, at least not onscreen. The original team was formed in 2012’s titular team-up movie, and then they returned in Age of Ultron three years later. But by the end of that film, a new line-up was formed – with Vision, Scarlet Witch, Falcon and War Machine joining while Iron Man, Thor, Hulk and Hawkeye left (leaving just Captain America and Black Widow as the sole remaining OGs). And then the whole Sokovia Accords thing happened two movies after that, which sent all the heroes into disarray. By the time Avengers: Endgame rolled around, it kinda seemed like, well, everyone was an Avenger?
And that mindset could be continuing into Doomsday. Based on the end of Thunderbolts, the Avengers name is getting thrown around by a couple of different groups now. In that film’s post-credits scene , the new Sam Wilson-led Avengers team is mentioned… by the Thunderbolts, who are now also calling themselves the Avengers. “But we are the Avengers,” says Yelena Belova. “The government said so. How does Sam Wilson not understand that?” Bucky Barnes responds, “Well, he does have the shield.” Indeed, it’s as if the idea behind the Sokovia Accords is still lurking here – do the Avengers work for the government or are they an independent operation? Sounds like we’ll have both in Doomsday.
This lineup is also interesting in that it’s got a couple of members from the first two incarnations of the team in Thor (who apparently is back from outer space, where we last saw him in Thor: Love and Thunder) and Sam. And while Scott Lang has worked with the Avengers plenty, he was nevery officially a member before this – although his inclusion here makes a lot of sense considering his history with Sam. As for Joaquin Torres, he’s a newbie, having been Sam’s partner in Captain America: Brave New World, as is Shang-Chi (though we did see the latter hero catching up with some familiar faces in his debut film’s post-credits , namely Wong, Captain Marvel, and Bruce Banner).
If you saw Thunderbolts, you know that this team came about as a result of Julia Louis-Dreyfus’s Valentina Allegra de Fontaine recruiting various super-powered folks over the course of the past few Marvel Phases, only to then try to have them all kill each other at the start of that film. Instead, they teamed up and saved New York City by the time of the closing credits, and so de Fontaine seized the opportunity to grab the spotlight and announced that they’re the New Avengers. She also owns Avengers Tower now, so, you know, convenient.
But also revealed in the film’s post-credits scene is that the New Avengers are losing the public relations war that is going on between them and Sam’s Avengers. And Sam has even filed for copyright of the name “Avengers.” Meanwhile, Red Guardian proposes that the team call themselves the New Avengerz, with a “z”...
This is a team of mostly “punch and shoot” type heroes – only Ghost and Sentry have truly formidable powers. They’ll definitely need some help against Doctor Doom.
Newcomers to the big screen – well, this incarnation of them anyway – the Fantastic Four just showed up in the summer of 2025, and now we’re all expected to be excited to see them meet up with our favorite heroes from 18 years worth of MCU and another 18 years of X-Men movies? Just not happening, sorry.
That said, Reed Richards and the gang will apparently be uniquely placed to inform the Avengers and X-Men about who it is that they’re up against, since the trailers for Doomsday have made it clear that the FF and Doom have a history of some kind in the universe that they hail from. This was left open-ended in The Fantastic Four: First Steps. Additionally, that film ended with Doom visiting with Reed and Sue’s baby son Franklin , presumably with a plan to kidnap the child and utilize the child’s reality-shaping powers to his own end. We see in the “final” Doomsday trailer that the FF visit Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter in the past, so could they be there to warn the couple that their own son might be in danger too?
You just can’t keep a good X-Men team down! Well, until you finally reboot them once and for all, which is currently happening with the Jake Schreier-directed X-Men movie that’s already cast new actors to play the likes of Professor X, Cyclops, Jean Grey, Storm, and more. So the return of the late Patrick Stewart’s Xavier, James Marsden’s Cyclops, and the rest for Doomsday feels like a sort of bittersweet last stand, if you will, that will almost surely end with their destruction. Will it be worth it just to see them in their classic comics costumes? Yeah, probably.
Do these guys count as a team? Who’s to say! They are an organized group of super-types (albeit with tech-focused abilities for the most part), so we’re including them. You got a problem with that? Then take it to He Who Remains. (Actually, strike that last part.)
Will Robert Downey, Jr.’s Doom have a team in Doomsday? It seems safe to say yes, and we think we have an idea of who they may be, too. They’re freaking powerful, actually. We already noted that he apparently kidnapped Franklin Richards – a baby that literally brought his own mother back to life. Speaking of which… we recently saw Doctor Doom resurrect Wanda Maximoff from the dead . Coincidence? And then there’s Bruce Banner, who wasn’t literally dead, but maybe just feeling a wee bit dead inside after losing control of the Hulk for the umpteenth time in Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Yeah, Doom has grabbed/recruited him too.
Doom will also have the mysterious Latverian Witches working for him, plus those nasty mutant-hunting robotic Sentinels. Oh, and he always has Doombots ready to go. Now that’s a team.
In addition to the teams that we’ll see in Doomsday, there are certainly some notable names who were not, strictly speaking, on any specific team last time we saw them. You’ve got guys like Steve Rogers, who based on the trailers at least is going to be a big part of the movie. Namor is swimming around out there somewhere. Shuri, who is now the Black Panther, is also in the trailers. Kate Bishop actress Hailee Steinfeld recently confirmed that she’ll be in the film too, which has fans wondering if the long-rumored Young Avengers will finally come to be in Doomsday too. And rumors peg Daredevil, Wolverine, and at least one Spider-Man as showing up as well – but we’ll have to wait until December 18 to see how true that is, and what else is in store for Marvel fans…
